high.title: Missing certificate pinning leaves an active TLS bypass unmitigated
high.description:
Two findings in this app combine into a single exploitable path: "No network security config declared" and "TrustManager accepts every server certificate".

An attacker on the network path - a rogue Wi-Fi access point, a compromised router - presents any certificate and the app accepts it. Nothing else in the app would have caught this: pinning is precisely the mitigation that exists for a bypass like this one.

Attack path:
1. No certificate pinning or network security config is declared (AndroidManifest.xml).
2. TrustManager accepts every server certificate accepts any certificate at sources/edu/ksu/cs/benign/MyTrustManager.java:10.
3. HostnameVerifier accepts every hostname accepts any certificate at sources/edu/ksu/cs/benign/MyIntentService.java:41.
4. An attacker on the network path intercepts and reads or modifies traffic to those endpoints.
high.impact: An attacker on the network path - a rogue Wi-Fi access point, a compromised router - presents any certificate and the app accepts it. Nothing else in the app would have caught this: pinning is precisely the mitigation that exists for a bypass like this one.
high.recommendation: Fix the TLS bypass first - it is the actual defect. Then add certificate pinning (a network security config pin-set, or OkHttp's CertificatePinner) for the app's own endpoints, so a future regression like this one is still caught in transit rather than depending on this code path alone staying correct.

high.title: TrustManager accepts every server certificate
high.description: checkServerTrusted() has an empty body, so every certificate is accepted including attacker-supplied ones. The app implements a custom X509TrustManager that performs no validation of the server's certificate chain in checkServerTrusted. info.title: Lack of screenshot protection
info.description: The app does not set FLAG_SECURE on its activities, including ResponseActivity which displays server responses.
info.impact: Sensitive information displayed on the screen can be captured via screenshots or screen recordings by other apps or the user.
info.recommendation: Set FLAG_SECURE in onCreate() for activities that display sensitive information.

reasons: Screen contents not protected from capture. Without FLAG_SECURE, what a screen shows can end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview. That matters on screens showing credentials, card numbers or balances; on its own it is a hardening note.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 27 those defaults still permit cleartext HTTP (see the cleartext finding).
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.
Lack of certificate pinning is a hardening step that only becomes a vulnerability when paired with a specific sensitive data channel.
Confirmed as part of chain-001: Missing certificate pinning leaves an active TLS bypass unmitigated.

info.description: On targetSdk 27, any component with an intent-filter is exported unless it says otherwise.
info.recommendation: Raise targetSdkVersion to 31+ and declare android:exported explicitly on every filtered component.

reasons: Legacy platform behaviour from SDK levels. An SDK level is a statement about which platform defaults apply, not a defect. It is context for the findings that depend on those defaults - pair it with one of them.

warnings: Implicit export only applies below targetSdk 31; confirm the app's targetSdkVersion before treating this as exploitable.

info.description: targetSdk 27 predates API 28, where cleartext HTTP became opt-in. The app targets SDK version 27, which permits cleartext HTTP traffic by default.
info.impact: Network communication sent over HTTP is vulnerable to interception and modification by a MITM attacker.

reasons: Cleartext permitted by configuration. The flag permits HTTP; it does not show that anything is sent over it. Name a request that actually goes out in cleartext, and what it carries, and this is a genuine finding.
Permitting cleartext is a platform default for targetSdkVersion 27 and requires a specific HTTP request to be a vulnerability.
warnings: Cleartext is blocked by default from targetSdk 28; confirm the declared target and any network security config.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 22 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "edu.ksu.cs.benign". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task.
info.impact: On a device running Android 10 or lower, a malicious app can put a look-alike screen on top of this app's task, phishing credentials or keeping the real app from being shown.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.
